# Data visualization: why rows and columns were removed

`Data_Cleaning.Rmd` dropped every column with more than 400 missing values, then removed every game that still had a missing value. This heatmap rebuilds those steps on the raw data, with games in chronological order (2001 at the top, 2025 at the bottom).

```{r, message=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
library(ggplot2)

# same steps as Data_Cleaning.Rmd
raw <- read.csv("ncaa_mbb_2001-2025_full.csv")[1:1511, ]
years <- raw$year
raw <- raw[, !(names(raw) %in% c("name.1", "link.1", "name.2", "link.2",
                                 "point_diff", "year", "conf.1", "conf.2"))]

na_matrix <- is.na(raw)
col_na <- colSums(na_matrix)
dropped_cols <- names(col_na)[col_na > 400]
kept_cols <- names(col_na)[col_na <= 400]
rows_removed <- sum(rowSums(na_matrix[, kept_cols]) > 0)

# columns: kept first, dropped last, each sorted by number of NAs
col_order <- c(kept_cols[order(col_na[kept_cols])], dropped_cols[order(col_na[dropped_cols])])

heat <- expand.grid(game = seq_len(nrow(raw)), variable = seq_along(col_order))
heat$missing <- as.vector(na_matrix[, col_order])
heat$status <- ifelse(!heat$missing, "Present",
                      ifelse(col_order[heat$variable] %in% dropped_cols,
                             "Missing in a dropped column",
                             "Missing in a kept column (game removed)"))

year_starts <- match(unique(years), years)

ggplot(heat, aes(x = variable, y = game, fill = status)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Present" = "grey92",
                               "Missing in a dropped column" = "#E69F00",
                               "Missing in a kept column (game removed)" = "#0072B2")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = length(kept_cols) + 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = year_starts, labels = unique(years)) +
  labs(title = "Missing values in the March Madness data",
       subtitle = "Columns right of the dashed line were dropped",
       x = "Variables (sorted by number of missing values)", y = "Tournament year",
       fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), legend.position = "bottom")

cat(length(dropped_cols), "of", ncol(raw), "columns dropped;",
    rows_removed, "of", nrow(raw), "games removed;", nrow(raw) - rows_removed, "games kept\n")
```

- **Dropped columns (orange):** advanced stats such as pace, offensive rating and the opponent shooting splits are missing for every game from 2002 to 2009, which is more than 500 games.
- **Removed games (blue):** all of 2002 is missing fouls per game, and all of 2024 is missing the bench-minutes stats, so those two years go entirely. The remaining removed games are scattered single-game gaps.
- **Why not impute:** whole seasons are missing at once, so filling in values would mean inventing them rather than estimating a few gaps.

# Load data
```{r}
library(C50)
library(caret)

madness_train <- readRDS("training_data.rds")
madness_test <- readRDS("testing_data.rds")

# C5.0 needs a factor outcome
madness_train$winner <- as.factor(madness_train$winner)
madness_test$winner <- as.factor(madness_test$winner)
```

# Basic decision tree
```{r}
tree_model <- C5.0(winner ~ ., data = madness_train)

tree_pred <- predict(tree_model, madness_test)

tree_confusion <- confusionMatrix(tree_pred, madness_test$winner, positive = "1")
tree_confusion
```

# Which variables does the tree use?
```{r}
C5imp(tree_model)
```

# Improving the model: boosting
```{r}
boost_model <- C5.0(winner ~ ., data = madness_train, trials = 10)

boost_pred <- predict(boost_model, madness_test)

boost_confusion <- confusionMatrix(boost_pred, madness_test$winner, positive = "1")
boost_confusion
```

# Comparison
```{r}
tree_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Decision tree", "Boosted tree (10 trials)"),
  Accuracy = c(tree_confusion$overall["Accuracy"],
               boost_confusion$overall["Accuracy"]),
  Sensitivity = c(tree_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"],
                  boost_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
  Specificity = c(tree_confusion$byClass["Specificity"],
                  boost_confusion$byClass["Specificity"]),
  Kappa = c(tree_confusion$overall["Kappa"],
            boost_confusion$overall["Kappa"])
)
row.names(tree_comparison) <- NULL
tree_comparison
```

# Saving relevant data files
```{r}
# Probability that team 1 wins, one value per test game, in the same order as testing_data.rds
tree_prob_stacked <- as.vector(predict(boost_model, madness_test, type = "prob")[, "1"])
summary(tree_prob_stacked)

saveRDS(tree_prob_stacked, "tree_stacked_probability.rds")
saveRDS(boost_confusion, "tree_confusion.rds")
```
